newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RICHEMONT RISES, MIH SLIPS ON NETHOLD DEAL.
newsitem.headline: RICHEMONT RISES, MIH SLIPS ON NETHOLD DEAL.

text.p: Industrial holding firm Richemont, which is based in Switzerland but South African controlled, saw its shares rise on Monday after a television deal announced on Friday.

At noon, Richemont shares were up 225 cents to 71.75 rand as analysts said the move would cut exposure to a loss-making part of the group. Shares which changed hands in the morning session were valued at 23.9 million rand.
"It is positive for Richemont because we are looking at losses dwindling," said one analyst.
The deal, announced in Paris on Friday, sees Canal Plus buy 100 percent of pay-television group Nethold from Richemont and MIH Holdings Ltd for $45 million cash and 6.1 million new Canal Plus shares.

Following the deal Richemont and MIH will own 15 and five percent of Canal Plus respectively. Nethold had been posting losses with investors eyeing its future potential, not current earnings, analysts said.
They said the deal cut Richemont's exposure to risk by giving it a smaller slice of a bigger established media firm.

But MIH shares were down 620 cents to 20 rand in early trade before settling at 320 cents lower at 23 rand at noon as speculative investors had placed a lot of store on the potential of MIH's stake in NetHold.
Analysts said that MIH's market value, in contrast to sprawling holding firm Richemont, had been strongly linked with the possible future profits to be reaped from its Nethold stake.
Now that the firm has replaced that with a smaller holding in Canal Plus it is a less exciting prospect, analysts said.
Omni Media Corp Ltd , which owns 35 percent of MIH, saw its shares drop 200 cents to 76 rand.
Newpaper reports have said that the deal saw Nethold snapped up for a bargain price, but analysts said it was too early in the group's development to make such a judgement.
"Values on media companies are difficult, especially ones that are not making a profit. It is unfair to say it is a bargain price. It is probably quite realistic," said one analyst.
